CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · 19 SAFETY CARDS

Staying Safe.

HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Nineteen rules, rehearsed until they are reflexes.

Every card in this class is one safety rule YOU can own: buckle up, hold hands near roads, red means stop, cross on the zebra, stop-look-listen, stop at the edge, walking feet, wear a helmet, give dogs space, don’t touch, hot things, medicine is not candy, fire safety, stop-drop-roll, and the helping spine — stop, ask, tell — with ask-for-help, if-you’re-lost, stay-with-your-group and tell-if-you’re-hurt finishing the set. Each card opens its own short page: the card itself, the rule it prints, one way to practise it today, and a link back to this page.

One card a sitting is plenty — the whole class is a term of five-minute safety talks, and the order runs road first, home second, fire third and people last. Safety is the one subject where rehearsal is the lesson: a rule you say at a calm curb is the rule that plays back at a busy one. Nothing here is scary. Everything here is said the way the cards say it — plainly, warmly, and with a grown-up’s hand somewhere in the picture.

WHY REHEARSAL WINS

A rule practised calmly is a rule that holds.

Safety teachers agree on the method: name the rule, act it out, and repeat it in the real place — the curb, the car, the kitchen. Fear teaches nothing; a drilled routine teaches everything. That is why this class runs on tiny repetitions done cheerfully, one card a week if that is the pace you and your grown-up choose, and why every page ends in something to DO, not just something to know.

The deck’s quiet center is the Safety Hero card: STOP, ASK, TELL. Every other rule in the set hangs off that spine — stop before the street, ask before touching, tell when something is wrong. If you keep only three words from this class, those are the three, and the card to hang on the fridge is Safety Hero.

THE ROAD SHELF · CARS, CROSSINGS AND BIKES

Out and about: the road shelf.

Nine cards for every walk, ride and drive: buckle up before the wheels turn, hold hands near roads, read the traffic lights, cross on the zebra, stop-look-listen at the curb, stop at the edge, keep your walking feet on the sidewalk, wear a helmet on wheels, and give every dog its space. Tap any card to open its page!

Buckle UpHold Hands Near RoadsTraffic LightsZebra CrossingStop, Look, ListenStop at the EdgeWalk, Don’t RunWear a HelmetSafe Distance
THE HOME SHELF · HOT, PLUGGED-IN, MEDICINE

Indoors: the home shelf.

Three cards for the house: sockets and plugs are don’t-touch, steam and stoves are hot things, and medicine is not candy — the grown-up hands it over, nobody else. Tap any card to open its page!

Don’t TouchHot ThingsMedicine Is Not Candy
THE FIRE SHELF · KNOW IT, DRILL IT

Fire: know it, drill it.

Two cards that rehearse the scary minute so nobody meets it cold: fire safety (notice it, get out, tell a grown-up) and the stop-drop-roll drill every four-year-old can own. Tap any card to open its page!

Fire SafetyStop, Drop, Roll
THE HELPING SHELF · PEOPLE WHO KEEP YOU SAFE

People: the helping shelf.

Five cards for the moments that need another person: the safety-hero spine (stop, ask, tell), asking for help from a trusted grown-up, what to do if you’re lost, staying with your group, and telling someone when you’re hurt. Tap any card to open its page!

Safety HeroAsk for HelpIf You’re LostStay with Your GroupTell If You’re Hurt
AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where this class fits.

Back to the Learning Path ↗Class 32 · Life Skills & Good Habits ↗Class 33 · Community Helpers & Our Neighborhood ↗Class 24 · Transportation & Vehicles ↗First Glance · the Staying-safe sheet ↗The parents’ shelf in the library · All 19 cards to print ↗

Class 32 builds the everyday habits this class keeps safe, Class 33 names the helpers a four-year-old can call on — firefighters, police officers, crossing guards — and Class 24 spots the vehicles whose rules this class rehearses. The First Glance safety sheet holds the same words as pictures, ready for the youngest sibling. And when the cards need printing, parents will find the whole deck on the parents’ shelf in the flashcards library — download and print buttons under every card, no extra pages to hop through.

Age ranges are a guide, not a test. Start with the rules your week already meets — the car, the curb, the kitchen — and let the card pages do the rehearsing with you.
